documents.title: What we do (and what we don't)
documents.content:
Check-ups and scale + polish. Hygienist in Tuesday, Wednesday and the Saturdays we're open.
White composite fillings. We stopped using amalgam in 2023.
Crowns and bridges - two appointments, about three weeks apart while the lab makes it.
Root canals on front teeth and premolars. Molars we normally refer.
Extractions. Wisdom teeth only if they're straightforward, otherwise it's the hospital.
Home whitening with custom trays. No in-chair whitening, we don't have the lamp.
Emergencies - two slots held every weekday morning. Ring at 8.15, they go fast.

Not us: implants, braces / Invisalign, veneers. All referred out.

documents.title: Policies
documents.content:
Cancellations
24 hours notice, otherwise it's £40. We waive it first time and we waive it if someone is genuinely ill - use your judgement, but write it on the card.

Deposits
£50 on anything booked for over an hour, and on any new patient booking after two no-shows. It comes off the final bill.

Turning up late
More than 15 minutes and we'll usually have to rebook. It isn't us being awkward, the next patient is already sitting there. Ring ahead and we'll do what we can.

NHS and private
The adult NHS list has been closed since 2024, with no date for reopening. NHS children under 18 we are still taking on, as long as one parent is on our private list.
Denplan and Bupa Dental Cover we invoice direct. Any other insurer, you pay us and claim it back - we'll do an itemised receipt.

documents.title: Things people ring up and ask
documents.content:
Do you do emergency appointments?
Two slots held every weekday morning. Phone at 8.15. Out of hours it's 111.

Can I just turn up?
No, everything's booked. You're welcome to wait on the off chance of a cancellation but don't bank on it.

Can I book online?
Not yet. It's on the list. Phone, or the form on the website.

Child's knocked a tooth out - what do we do?
Ring us straight away. Keep the tooth in milk and don't scrub it.

Can I bring my toddler to my own appointment?
Yes, but there's nobody on reception to watch them and the surgery is small. Bring another adult if you possibly can.

Do you do implants?
No. We refer to Mr Adeyemi at Cheadle - he does the surgery, we do the crown on top afterwards.

Can I have my records or my x-rays?
Yes. Put it in writing, email is fine, and give us up to a month. No charge.

How often should I be coming?
Depends on the mouth. Some people six months, some three, some once a year. The dentist tells you at the exam.

I'm really nervous about coming in, what happens?
Your first visit is booked as a double slot so nobody is rushed, and it can be talking only if that's all you can manage. Tell Denise when you book and she flags it on the card. We don't do IV sedation here - that's the practice on Barlow Moor Road.

How can I pay?
Card, cash or Apple Pay. We don't take cheques.

How do I make a complaint?
In writing to the practice manager, Denise Whitaker. We reply inside 10 working days. If you're still not happy after that it goes to the Dental Complaints Service and we'll give you the number.

documents.title: How we write back
documents.content:
Warm, short, plain English. We're a small practice on a busy road, not a call centre.
First name if they've given us one.
Never diagnose in writing. Pain, swelling or anything that sounds like an infection - get them on the phone, don't go back and forth in messages.
Prices are always "from". Never quote a final figure before the dentist has looked.
A lot of the people messaging us are frightened and have been putting it off for years. Don't be brisk with them. "That's really common, we see it every week" does more than anything else you could write.
Complaints - say sorry for the experience, don't admit fault, give them Denise's name and get it off the public thread.
Sign off from the practice: "Brightside Dental, Withington". No exclamation marks in review replies.
